rationale: lendzy.co.uk has three tool pages that serve HTTP 200 to every visitor and are recorded in pages as never built (build_status='needs_rebuild', deployed_at IS NULL). Both readings are correct: the artefact deployed on 2026-08-02 is still in the bucket, while the record was never advanced. Root cause, read at the deciding arm: each page carries a SINGLE page_components row (written 2026-08-02 by the original shadow build) with component_id NULL and slot_name 'section'. resolveComponent (rerender_page_sections_action.go:361) resolves a section by component_id first and slot_name second; the id is empty (COALESCE at :924) and no content_components row is named, functioned or typed 'section' (verified 0 rows), so the slot enters UnresolvedSlots, rerenderResolution.fatal() (:650) fails the step, the page never reaches build_status='deployed', and UpdatePageStatusAction (v3_site_actions.go:1082) only stamps deployed_at inside that branch. It cannot self-heal: needs_rebuild re-selects the page, the render fails identically, and six page_rerender items since 2026-08-25 all read complete. The unstamped rows then fail datahelpers.NeverDeployedPagePredicate, which drops the three URLs from the sitemap (27 <loc> against 30 active pages) and files 47 unbuilt_internal_link items at needs_human_review — none of which is a broken link; every target serves 200. The owner's instruction is to keep working tools, so this repairs by ADOPTION, not regeneration: create_tool_component builds from LLM-generated HTML and would replace three working calculators. Instead the live stored HTML is promoted to html_template, which is lossless because all three bodies contain zero '{{' bindings — the measurement that licenses the approach, and Guard 3 re-asserts it at apply time rather than trusting it. Filed to the 090 loop before assertion per the 2026-07-31 owner ruling: intake 1ff4c475, run 89a84ad3.

plan.summary: ROUND 3, answering all four round-2 findings with measurement. (a) The gating HIGH was real twice over: the rerender INSERT omitted the FIRST-CLASS page_id column (the live producer sets it on all 7,481 of its rows [MEASURED 2026-09-02]) and omitted created_by, which is NOT NULL with NO DEFAULT — round 2 would have ERRORED at apply. Both columns now set (page_id=p.id, created_by='lendzy_co_uk lane (migration 693)') and the verify asserts page_id IS NOT NULL on the queued rows. (b) The named prior class is bugs_open/357 (whole tools stored under a FALSE component identity, one row per page; OWNED, active session, 090 run 63d4d1a7 pending): their arm is a WRONG component_id (hero) where regeneration is the disaster and the park is load-bearing; ours is a NULL component_id where deployment is impossible and regeneration is harmless — adoption makes the declared template BYTE-IDENTICAL to the stored tool, so 357's §3 hazard structurally cannot fire here. Cited in the header and CONTRIB'd to their session. (c) bug_historian's resolution question is answered with the PRODUCTION function: all three adopted bodies PASS toolTemplateValid (the guard loadComponentSchemasByID applies at component_level='tool') and a >100-char truncated control is REJECTED in the same run, via a one-shot in-package test. (d) The 47 unbuilt_internal_link items are deliberately NOT hand-retracted: RegisterVerifier('unbuilt_internal_link', VerifyUnbuiltInternalLinkResolved) judges by NeverDeployedPagePredicate, so revalidation resolves them once the pages stamp; hand-closing them would blind the mechanism that filed them. A POST-CONDITIONS block gives the operator the async acceptance queries (deployed_at x3; artefact input counts unchanged 3/1/2; sitemap 30 <loc>; the 47 falling to 0). Everything else is unchanged from round 2.
plan.risks: Round 1's risks (1)-(4) and (6) stand unchanged (function collision guarded per RFC_036 9.3; racing another session's repair guarded; lossy adoption guarded on zero '{{' bindings; acceptance is at the ARTEFACT with unchanged <input> counts 3/1/2 as the control that no working calculator was swapped; verification is DO/RAISE throughout because bare SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT). ROUND 1's RISK (5) IS NOW A CHANGE, NOT A RISK — that was the gating objection. Two new risks it introduces: (7) Stacking a second live rerender on a page that already has one queued. Guarded: the new DO block aborts with a readable reason if any non-terminal row carries these item_keys, which also turns what would be an idx_swi_dedup 23505 into a stated abort. (8) Rollback racing a handler. The rollback cancels ONLY rows still at 'triaged'; a claimed or complete rerender is deliberately left alone, because cancelling a row a handler is already acting on does not stop the handler, it only makes the record lie. Round 1's framing is also CORRECTED by the council's own read-only check, and the correction is in the migration header: page_rerender items ARE filed against these pages periodically (20+ on 2026-09-01 10:45 from source 'rerender-pages'), so 'needs_rebuild has no consumer' was too strong for this site — the items are filed and then FAIL. Filing our own is therefore belt-and-braces rather than the only route, and it is still correct: relying on another scheduled batch to notice is how a repair sits inert for a fortnight and reads as done.

edits.rationale: The change. Guards 1-3 assert the three preconditions (no library-tool function collision; exactly 3 rows still unrepaired; zero template bindings in the bodies being adopted), each as DO/RAISE so a violated precondition aborts. The INSERT creates one tool component per page from that page's own pc.rendered_html, joined to a VALUES list supplying display_name and description. The UPDATE repoints component_id and corrects slot_name from the generic 'section' to the tool function, which is the shape the six healthy siblings carry and which makes the slot_name fallback route resolve as well as the id route. The verify block re-runs the lane's founding query fleet-wide, so it fails if ANY active page anywhere is left with no identified component on any row. ROUND 2 ADDS SECTION 4: a guard refusing to stack on a live queued row, then one INSERT filing a page_rerender per page with handler_agent 'page-rerender', priority 80, status 'triaged' (the status idx_swi_handler indexes for pickup) and a spec carrying domain, page_id, filename (ltrim(p.url,'/')) and page_name — the shape measured from this site's own rows. The verify block gains a fourth assertion, 3 queued rerenders, so the failure mode the council caught cannot recur silently.
edits.sketch:
DO $$ ... IF n <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '693 ABORT: % library tool row(s) already claim one of these functions — this migration must fork, not insert (RFC_036 9.3)', n; END IF; END $$;
INSERT INTO content_components (name, display_name, description, html_template, function,
    section_type, component_level, category, render_mode, created_from, is_active,
    forked_from, suitable_site_types, suitable_page_types)
SELECT p.name || '-lendzy-co-uk', d.display_name, d.description, pc.rendered_html, p.name,
       NULL, 'tool', 'interactive', 'template', 'adopted', true, NULL, '[]'::jsonb, '[]'::jsonb
  FROM pages p JOIN page_components pc ON pc.page_id = p.id
  JOIN (VALUES ('tool-price-cap-checker', 'Price cap checker', '...'), ...) AS d(page_name, display_name, description)
    ON d.page_name = p.name
 WHERE p.site_id = '8ff093d5-...' AND pc.component_id IS NULL;
UPDATE page_components pc SET component_id = cc.id, slot_name = p.name, updated_at = NOW()
  FROM pages p, content_components cc
 WHERE pc.page_id = p.id AND cc.function = p.name AND pc.component_id IS NULL ...;
-- ROUND 2, section 4:
DO $$ ... IF n <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '693 ABORT: % live page_rerender item(s) already queued for these pages', n; END IF; END $$;
INSERT INTO site_work_items (site_id, item_type, item_key, status, handler_agent, priority, source, summary, spec)
SELECT p.site_id, 'page_rerender', 'page_rerender_' || p.name || '_' || p.site_id || '_assemble', 'triaged',
       'page-rerender', 80, 'lendzy_co_uk lane (migration 693)', 'Rerender page: ' || p.name,
       jsonb_build_object('domain','lendzy.co.uk','page_id',p.id::text,'filename',ltrim(p.url,'/'),'page_name',p.name, 'reason','component adopted by migration 693')
  FROM pages p WHERE p.site_id='8ff093d5-...' AND p.name IN (the three);
-- verify gains: IF queued <> 3 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION '693 VERIFY: expected 3 queued rerenders, found % — the repair would be inert', queued; END IF;

edits.rationale: Restores component_id NULL / slot_name 'section' and deletes the three adopted rows, with its own DO/RAISE verify. Its header states plainly that rolling back RESTORES THE DEFECT, and warns that if the framework has already stamped deployed_at and shipped new bytes, a blind rollback leaves the record pointing at nothing while a newer artefact serves — worse than either side — with the query to check that first. ROUND 2: also cancels rerenders this migration queued that are still at 'triaged', and only those.

grounded_in: rerender_page_sections_action.go:361-394 resolveComponent — 'if s.componentID != "" { if ci, ok := byID[s.componentID]; ok { return ci, false, true } ... } if ci, ok := schemas[s.slotName]; ok { return ci, false, true } return componentInfo{}, false, false' — both routes fail for a row with a NULL id and a slot_name matching no component.

rerender_page_sections_action.go:650 — 'func (r rerenderResolution) fatal() bool { return len(r.UnresolvedSlots) > 0 || len(r.InvalidTemplateSlots) > 0 }', and :600 returns an error on fatal(), so the step fails rather than completing.
v3_site_actions.go:1082 — buildPageDeployStampQuery is called only inside 'if newStatus == "deployed"', so a page that never reaches that status can never be stamped.
render_sitemap_action.go:144 — 'AND deployed_at IS NOT NULL', which is why the three unstamped URLs are absent from a sitemap that carries 27 <loc> against 30 active pages [MEASURED 2026-09-02].

datahelpers NeverDeployedPagePredicateFor — 'deployed_at IS NULL AND COALESCE(build_status,'') <> 'deployed'' — one definition consumed by both the sitemap filter and the unbuilt-link check, which is why one unstamped row produces both symptoms.

[MEASURED 2026-09-02] Fleet-wide query 'HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE pc.component_id IS NOT NULL) = 0' over active pages returns exactly lendzy's three tool pages, all needs_rebuild and unstamped, and nothing else in the estate.

[MEASURED 2026-09-02] content_components has 0 rows whose function or section_type matches these three tools, so no library row is being shadowed and Guard 1 is currently satisfiable.

UpdatePageStatusAction only stamps deployed_at when a rerender succeeds and reaches the deployed branch — the diagnosis's cited fix for the sitemap-exclusion and unbuilt_internal_link symptoms depends on that branch firing, and no edit causes it to fire.'

[MEASURED 2026-09-02] The shape filed by the live producer on this very site: item_key 'page_rerender_tool-price-cap-checker_8ff093d5-...-_assemble', handler_agent 'page-rerender', priority 80, source 'rerender-pages', spec {domain, page_id, filename 'tools/price-cap-checker/index.html', page_name}.

idx_swi_dedup is UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) WHERE item_key IS NOT NULL AND status <> ALL (complete, verified, rejected, wont_fix, failed, unresolved, cancelled) — so re-filing a key whose prior rows are 'complete' is permitted, and only a LIVE row collides.
idx_swi_handler is btree (handler_agent, status) WHERE status = ANY (triaged, approved) — which is why the new rows are born 'triaged' rather than any other status.

The council's own round-1 read-only check, which CORRECTS this submission's round-1 claim that needs_rebuild has no consumer: 20+ page_rerender rows created 2026-09-01 10:45 against these three pages, all reaching 'complete' while the pages stayed needs_rebuild and unstamped.

[MEASURED 2026-09-02] site_work_items.page_id is a first-class column and created_by is NOT NULL with no default; SELECT page_id IS NOT NULL, count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='page_rerender' AND source='rerender-pages' GROUP BY 1 returns t|7481 — every producer row carries it.
